title: Next Greater Element II
statement: The list is circular: after the last element comes the first again. For each element return the next strictly greater value found while moving forward (wrapping around at most once), or -1 if none exists.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(32)
    return [[r.randint(0, 10**6) for _ in range(100000)]]

hints.1_question: A circular array can be thought of as the array written twice. How could you reuse the usual next-greater stack idea?
hints.2_nudge: Loop i from 0 to 2n-1 using nums[i % n]. Only push indices during the first pass.
hints.3_big_hint: For i in range(2n): x = nums[i % n]; while stack and nums[stack[-1]] < x: res[pop] = x; if i < n: push i.

known_bugs.name: single pass (ignores the wrap-around)
known_bugs.followup: For [3, 2, 1], what is the next greater element of 2 if you may wrap around to the start?

known_bugs.name: pops on equal values (<=)
known_bugs.followup: The next greater element must be strictly greater. Is an equal value greater?

known_bugs.name: scans forward from every index (O(n^2))
known_bugs.followup: For a value that is the maximum, how many elements does your scan look at? Can a stack share that work between indices?

followups: Why do you push indices only in the first pass?
What would change if you needed the next smaller element instead?
